title: (No AI) Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
Carl Pei via X" data-has-syndication-rights="1" src="https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/nothing.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100" />

Nothing's [new AI device](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1038405/nothing-screen-free-ai-device-announce-december-8) is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple's [new Watch feature](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1037100/apple-siri-recap-audio-intelligence-hands-on) and devices like [Amazon's Bee wearable](https://www.theverge.com/column/1026464/optimizer-amazon-bee-frontier-ambient-listening-wearables). Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-23/phone-maker-nothing-to-launch-ear-note-earbuds-and-case-with-ai-recording), but said the company hasn't yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th.

The report also says Nothing's [rumored plans](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/1010996/nothing-is-reportedly-launching-two-pairs-of-smart-glasses-including-an-audio-only-model) for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be "pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next y …

title: (No AI) Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
![A faceless mannequin with digital embellishments against a colorful background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/06/STK419_DEEPFAKE_CVIRGINIA_F.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, [Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield](https://www.doj.state.or.us/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ODOJ-Grok-Complaint-Final-Submitted-2026-11-22.pdf) and [Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones](https://www.oag.state.va.us/files/Grok-SpaceX-Complaint-As-Filed.pdf) accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The [complaint filed in Virginia](https://www.oag.state.va.us/files/Grok-SpaceX-Complaint-As-Filed.pdf) accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and "instead saw a market opportunity for more profits," describing the weak safeguards around Grok as "not a failure but a feature."
